issues.legal_issue: Dispensing with the landowners’ opportunity to object is unjustified when land is acquired for planned residential development and the government does not establish a real urgency requiring the inquiry to be eliminated.
material_facts: The acquisition was for a planned residential colony.
The land-selection process began years before the acquisition notifications, and there was a further delay of more than a year between the notifications and the declaration of acquisition.
The government produced no material showing that it had applied its mind to whether the urgency required eliminating the landowners’ opportunity to object.
The development authority sought the land in part because it lacked a land bank and wished to keep the authority running.
issues.conclusion: The use of urgency powers to dispense with the inquiry was unjustified, and the notifications were legally infirm to the extent that they excluded the inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4(1), 5A, 17(1), 17(1A) and 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, read together, require the government to consider not only whether urgency exists but also whether it is so pressing that the summary inquiry must be dispensed with. The right to object under Section 5A is valuable and may be removed only for good reason supported by material and after application of mind. Planned residential or urban development ordinarily allows time for an expedited inquiry; dispensing with it for such development is exceptional, not routine. The Court followed Narayan Govind Gavate v. State of Maharashtra and Union of India v. Mukesh Hans, and agreed with Om Prakash v. State of U.P. that State of U.P. v. Pista Devi could not establish a contrary general rule. It also considered the principles in Gurdial Singh, Rajasthan Housing Board, and other cited decisions concerning urgency and judicial review.

rule.if: challenge_to_compulsory_acquisition and residential_planned_development and (extended_pre_or_post_notification_delay or no_evidence_of_mind_applied_to_waiver)

predicates.challenge_to_compulsory_acquisition: A landowner challenged compulsory acquisition proceedings and the removal of the opportunity to object.
predicates.residential_planned_development: The land was acquired for planned residential or urban development.
predicates.extended_pre_or_post_notification_delay: The acquisition process included a substantial delay before the notification, after it, or both.
predicates.no_evidence_of_mind_applied_to_waiver: The government did not place material before the court showing that it considered whether urgency required eliminating the owners’ opportunity to object.
predicates.dispensing_with_owner_objections_unjusti: The government’s decision to remove the owners’ opportunity to object was unjustified.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns compulsory acquisition for planned residential development and there was substantial delay or no evidence that the government considered the need to eliminate objections, dispensing with those objections is unjustified.

issues.legal_issue: An unjustified dispensation of the inquiry does not require the acquisition to be undone when implementation is substantially complete and most affected owners have accepted compensation.
material_facts: The inquiry had been improperly dispensed with, but an award had been made.
More than 370 of approximately 400 landowners had accepted compensation.
The development authority had spent a substantial part of the development cost and completed more than 60 percent of the work.
The appellants and a small number of other owners had not accepted compensation.
issues.conclusion: Despite the legal infirmity in dispensing with the inquiry, the appellants were not entitled to relief undoing the acquisition in the circumstances, and the appeals were dismissed subject to liberty to make representations concerning release of their land.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the legal defect in dispensing with the inquiry did not, in the peculiar circumstances, warrant setting aside the acquisition after substantial implementation and widespread acceptance of compensation. The judgment applies the Court’s assessment of the consequences of relief in light of the facts, rather than treating the invalidity of the dispensation as automatically requiring the completed acquisition to be undone.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_compulsory_acquisition and inquiry_improperly_waived and award_made and most_owners_accepted_compensation and substantial_development_completed

predicates.appeal_challenging_compulsory_acquisitio: Landowners brought an appeal challenging compulsory acquisition proceedings.
predicates.inquiry_improperly_waived: The government removed the owners’ opportunity to object without adequate justification.
predicates.award_made: An award determining compensation had been made.
predicates.most_owners_accepted_compensation: Most of the affected owners accepted the compensation offered for their land.
predicates.substantial_development_completed: A substantial portion of the planned development had been completed.
predicates.acquisition_not_undone_despite_invalid_w: The acquisition is not undone notwithstanding the unjustified removal of the owners’ opportunity to object.

issues.definition: If an appeal challenges compulsory acquisition, the objection opportunity was improperly removed, an award was made, most owners accepted compensation, and substantial development was completed, the acquisition is not undone despite that defect.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not direct release of land when the claimed pre-acquisition structures are disputed, but may allow the owners to seek withdrawal from acquisition and require the government to consider their request without discrimination.
material_facts: The appellants claimed that houses, structures, and buildings existed on their land before the acquisition notifications and sought release of the land under the State’s policy.
The development authority disputed that claim and asserted that the structures had been built after the notifications.
Possession of the appellants’ land had not been taken.
The appellants also alleged that other land had been released while theirs had not been considered for release.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to direct release of the land because the timing of the structures was disputed. It permitted the appellants to make representations seeking release and directed the State to consider any timely representation according to law and State policy, without discrimination.
issues.legal_principle: Section 48(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 gives the government liberty to withdraw from acquisition. Because the existence and timing of the claimed structures were seriously disputed, the Court did not decide that the land must be released. Since possession had not been taken, it allowed the appellants to seek release through a representation and required its consideration in accordance with law and State policy, without discrimination.

rule.if: challenge_to_compulsory_acquisition and claimed_pre_acquisition_structures_disputed and possession_not_taken and owner_requests_release

predicates.claimed_pre_acquisition_structures_dispu: The owners claimed that structures predated the acquisition notice, while the acquiring authority disputed when those structures were built.
predicates.possession_not_taken: The acquiring authority had not taken possession of the owners’ land.
predicates.owner_requests_release: The owners asked for their land to be released from the acquisition.
predicates.owner_may_seek_release_by_representation: The owners may seek release by representation, which the government must consider without discrimination and in accordance with its policy and the law.

issues.definition: When owners challenge compulsory acquisition, the timing of claimed structures is disputed, possession has not been taken, and release is sought, they may request release by representation for non-discriminatory consideration.
